key: wedding reception in Kochi, an uncle
name: ch10_wedding_wrong_score
alt: At a wedding reception an uncle happily tells a cricket story while the young listener keeps a scorecard folded in his pocket and laughs along.
scene: A wide view of a lively wedding reception hall in Kochi in the evening, strings of marigold garlands and small fairy lights along the back wall, round tables with white cloths and banana-leaf plates of biryani. In the CENTRE, a cheerful uncle in his sixties (cream mundu, light shirt, thick moustache, spectacles) stands with one arm raised high, mid-story, beaming. A speech bubble above him shows a tiny cricket bat and the number "100". Seated beside him on the LEFT, a middle-aged mother in a green silk sari glances sideways with a nervous smile. Around the table three more relatives laugh and clap. On the RIGHT, a young man of about 25 (blue kurta) sits laughing politely with one hand on his chest; his other hand is pressing a small folded paper back into his kurta pocket, and a thin dashed arrow points from the pocket to a little calendar inset in the top-right corner showing a closed scorecard and a clock, meaning the correction waits for another day. A faint thought bubble above the young man shows a tiny scorecard with a cross over it. Warm golden light, festive and kind mood: the evening matters more than the fact. Labels: "LAUGH ALONG" above the young man, "LATER" above the small calendar inset in the top-right.

key: Two neighbours in a Delhi housing society
name: ch10_society_parking_win
alt: A split picture: a neighbour wins a parking argument on his phone, then a week later the other family turns away from him and the society feels cold.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, set in a Delhi housing society with cream apartment blocks and an iron gate. LEFT panel: a man in his forties (white polo shirt, spectacles) stands beside a society gate holding his phone up triumphantly; a big phone screen inset floats next to him showing a group chat with three message bubbles: a photo of a car, a clock icon and a small rule sheet, plus a green tick. Across the gate a grey hatchback is parked crooked. In the background his neighbour (a man in his thirties, maroon shirt) stands with his phone lowered and his head down, silent. Label "WON" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the same society a week later, the same winner standing alone in the courtyard looking puzzled; behind him the neighbour turns his back, holding the hands of two small children who are walking away from the winner's son, who stands alone holding a cricket ball. A domestic helper with a bucket looks the other way. A small notice board in the corner shows "MEETING" with a frosty blue tint and tiny icicles drawn on its edges, meaning every meeting will now be cold. Cool afternoon light on the right, bright light on the left. Labels: "WON" over the left panel, "LOST GOODWILL" over the right panel.

key: Tug-of-war at a school sports day
name: ch10_tug_of_war_let_go
alt: A split picture of a school tug-of-war: both teams straining with the rope stuck, then one side lets go and the other team stumbles while the first child walks over to talk.
scene: A split-panel scene on a dusty Indian school ground on sports day, white chalk lines, a few coloured bunting flags on a rope in the background. LEFT panel: two teams of school children in uniform (white shirts, one side with blue sashes, the other with red sashes) lean back hard on a thick jute rope, faces scrunched, heels dug into the ground; a red ribbon tied at the middle of the rope sits exactly over the chalk centre line, and two thick opposing arrows show both pulls, cancelling. A small "=" badge floats above the ribbon. Label "PULL" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the blue-sash boy at the front (about 12, neat hair) has opened his hands and dropped the rope, which lies slack on the ground in a loose curve; the red team tumbles backwards into a heap, surprised but laughing, dust puffs around them. The blue boy is already walking forward with an open palm held out in greeting, a small speech bubble with three dots above him to show he is ready to talk. A teacher with a whistle watches from the edge, smiling. Bright midday sunshine, cheerful mood. Labels: "PULL" over the left panel, "LET GO" over the right panel.

key: A scooter at a Chennai junction has
name: ch10_scooter_right_of_way
alt: A scooter rider at a junction with a green light brakes hard as a large water tanker rolls through the red light in front of him.
scene: A street-level view of a busy Chennai road junction in hot morning light, a traffic signal pole on the LEFT showing a bright green light for the rider and, on a second signal head facing the cross street, a red light. In the LEFT foreground a young man of about 28 (light blue office shirt, black helmet, backpack) rides a grey scooter towards the junction. In the CENTRE and RIGHT, a large blue water tanker truck with a round tank and a dripping tap at the back rolls across the junction from right to left, clearly ignoring its red signal. Two choices are shown as thin branching dashed arrows from the scooter's front wheel: one arrow goes straight ahead into the side of the tanker and ends at a small inset bubble with a hospital bed and a red cross; the other arrow curves to a stop line where the rider has squeezed his brakes, ending at a green tick. A small shield floating above the rider's helmet shows a tiny green light symbol, cracked down the middle, meaning being right is not armour. Palm trees and a tea stall blur in the background. Tense but clear mood. Labels: "RIGHT" next to the cracked shield, "BRAKE" beside the green tick at the stop line.

key: You are at the RTO office in Bengaluru
name: ch10_rto_clerk_respect
alt: A split picture at a government office counter: arguing makes the clerk fold his arms, asking his advice makes him smile and fix the form with a pen.
scene: A split-panel illustration set at the same government transport office counter, a wooden counter with a steel grille window, files stacked high, a ceiling fan and a wall clock. LEFT panel: a young woman of about 30 (yellow kurta, sling bag, phone in hand) leans forward, one finger jabbing at a form on the counter, a speech bubble showing a tiny laptop screen. Behind the grille, a middle-aged clerk (grey safari shirt, spectacles, moustache) sits back with arms tightly folded and a stern face; a small red cross badge floats above the form. A small calendar icon reading "tomorrow" hangs near him. Label "ARGUE" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the same woman stands upright, hands open in a respectful gesture, a gentle smile, a speech bubble with a small question mark. The clerk now leans forward with a relaxed smile, holding a pen and making a correction on her form, while his other hand points knowingly at a tiny laptop icon with a cross on it, as if explaining the website's mistake. A green tick badge floats above the form. Same warm office light, but the right panel feels friendlier. Labels: "ARGUE" over the left panel, "ASK HIS ADVICE" over the right panel.

key: A street dog lies across a narrow lane
name: ch10_street_dog_other_lane
alt: A man at a fork in old narrow lanes takes the longer side lane instead of pushing past a growling dog lying across his own lane.
scene: A view looking down two narrow old lanes in Varanasi at a fork, tall old buildings with peeling ochre and blue walls, small shrine niches, hanging electric wires and a strip of sky above. In the LEFT lane, a brown street dog lies stretched across the whole width of the paving, head up, teeth showing, small jagged growl marks beside its muzzle; a tiny inset bubble above the dog shows a bandaged hand and a syringe, meaning a bite and injections even if you win. A red dashed arrow from the man toward the dog ends in a small red cross. In the RIGHT lane, which bends gently away around a corner, a green dashed arrow curves from the man along the lane, past a doorway with a hanging bell, ending at a green tick; a small clock badge on the arrow reads "+2 min". In the CENTRE foreground at the fork stands a middle-aged man (white kurta, shoulder bag, carrying a cloth bag of vegetables), turning his body towards the right lane with a calm, slightly amused expression, one hand raised as if saying "fine". Soft late-afternoon light falling into the lanes. Labels: "MY LANE" above the left lane with the dog, "NEXT LANE" above the right lane.

key: A good umpire in a heated village cricket
name: ch10_umpire_calm_steps
alt: A village cricket umpire listens calmly to an upset batsman while a row of six small step icons shows how he handles the dispute.
scene: A wide view of a village cricket final on a dusty ground, a small crowd sitting on a low wall behind, a coconut tree and a tractor at the edge. In the CENTRE, an umpire of about 55 (white shirt, white cap, a towel over his shoulder) stands near the stumps with an open hand and a calm, attentive face, head slightly tilted to listen. Facing him on the LEFT, a batsman of about 25 (white clothes, pads, helmet pushed back, bat held loosely) gestures with frustration, a speech bubble with a jagged edge above him containing a small "!". On the RIGHT, at square leg, a second umpire stands a little away, and a thin dashed arrow links the two umpires to show checking with him. Behind the batsman the opposing captain stands with arms crossed but relaxed. Across the bottom of the picture runs a horizontal row of six small round icons joined by a line like beads, left to right: an ear, two overlapping circles, an open hand, a thinking cloud, a heart, and a teacup with a clock for the drinks break. Clear morning light, tense moment calming down. Labels: "LISTEN FIRST" above the umpire, "PLAY ON" at the end of the row of icons on the right.

key: A pressure cooker and its whistle again
name: ch10_one_cooker_at_a_time
alt: A split picture of a small kitchen: two cookers whistling at once make a confused noise, then one cooker whistles while the other is off the stove as the couple take turns.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same small Mumbai one-room-flat kitchen, a two-burner gas stove on a granite slab, steel utensils on a wall rack, a small window. LEFT panel: two pressure cookers sit on both burners, both whistling at once, two big tangled white steam clouds colliding above them with jagged noise lines; a husband of about 35 (grey vest) and a wife of about 33 (pink cotton sari) both cover their ears and shout at each other, each with a jagged speech bubble, and a big "?" badge floats between the cookers because nobody can tell which dal is ready. Label "BOTH AT ONCE" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: only one cooker sits on the stove, whistling a single neat plume of steam; the second cooker rests on the slab beside the stove, lid off, quiet. The wife speaks with open hands, a single speech bubble above her, while the husband sits on a low stool with his hands on his knees, leaning in and listening. A small circular swap arrow badge above them shows that they will change turns next. Calm warm evening light from the window on the right side. Labels: "BOTH AT ONCE" over the left panel, "ONE AT A TIME" over the right panel.
